title: Veridict Ledger Entry (Standard v1.0.0-draft, §4)
description: One append-only entry. Hash binding: entry_hash = sha256(canonical [prev_hash, payload, entry_type, seq, author, ts, schema_version]); payload_hash = sha256(canonical payload). ts is an ISO-8601 UTC STRING — floats are too fragile to hash across languages.

entry_type.description: Open registry. Core types, enumerated: key.enrolled, task.started, claim.registered, evidence.recorded, watch.observed, deliberation.rounded, escalation.requested, escalation.resolved, calibration.updated, gate.blocked, checkpoint.anchored, certificate.issued, watcher.registered, watcher.revoked, actor.output, dossier.opened, incident.recorded. The registry is open by design — an unknown type is legal — but extensions MUST be namespaced 'extension.*' so a verifier that does not recognize it can abstain rather than silently misparse the payload. Semantic consumers (totals, netting) MUST understand the core types before interpreting payloads; a charge and its refund are distinguished by entry type, not by payload field.

seq.description: Position in the chain; 0 is genesis.

kind.description: Open registry (§2.4): system, watcher, jury, human, agent — plus implementer-defined kinds (adjudicator, policy_engine, verifier...).

payload.description: Entry-type-specific; hashed as canonical JSON. Open schema — implementers may add entry types, but core semantics (§2.4) are fixed.
